title: Towards Ultra-High-Rate Quantum Error Correction with Reconfigurable Atom Arrays
abstract: Develops ultra-high-rate quantum error correcting codes co-designed with neutral atom (reconfigurable) hardware. Identifies structural conditions on affine permutation matrices that make encoding rates exceeding 1/2 compatible with efficient implementation, enabling syndrome extraction and atom rearrangement under realistic parallel control constraints. Demonstrated code instances: [[2304,1156,<=14]] at logical error rate 1.3e-13 per round, and [[1152,580,<=12]] at 2.9e-11 per round, both at physical noise p=0.1%. Approaches the teraquop regime.
key_claims: Encoding rates exceeding 50% achieved — substantially higher than typical ~10% surface code rates
[[2304,1156]] code achieves logical error rate 1.3e-13 per round at p=0.1% noise
Hardware co-design for neutral atom reconfigurable arrays (QuEra-style)
Approaches teraquop regime: 1 error per trillion operations
Relevant to Aquila-class hardware used in our HYP-017 design
hardware_used: Reconfigurable neutral atom arrays (QuEra Aquila class)
supports_or_contradicts: SUPPORTS — QEC breakthrough on the exact hardware class (QuEra neutral atoms) we targeted for HYP-017. Higher logical qubit counts at lower overhead increases future simulation capacity for MERA circuits on Aquila.
